---
title: "Figure conventions and reproducibility"
---

Documentation figures use **R and ggplot2**, with one shared theme in
`figures/style.R` and explicit figure jobs in `figures/render.R`. Rust/PHP
estimation has no graphics or R dependency. The .qmd walkthroughs still use
Python for matrices and independent verification; a small bridge passes computed
points to R for drawing. No ipynb files are maintained as documentation sources.

## Visual conventions

- Language comparisons keep **R, Python, PHP** in that order. Python is labeled
  statsmodels or SciPy reference to identify the actual implementation.
- R uses blue circles (#0072B2); Python uses orange triangles (#D55E00); PHP uses
  green squares (#009E73). Color and shape reinforce the labels.
- Conceptual figures use blue for the reference/population curve, green for the
  conditional/native curve, orange for an approximation or boundary, and gray for
  observations. Their legends describe the statistical quantity rather than imply
  that a curve is an implementation comparison.
- Use a white background, common sans-serif type, restrained grids and explicit
  quantity/unit labels. Titles state what is shown; captions state the data or
  approximation, transformations and relevant limits.
- Bar charts start at zero. Benchmark facets use their own labeled linear scales
  and show median bars plus actual timing repetitions. Missing memory is labeled
  unrecorded, not plotted as measured zero. A measured time of zero is marked 0*
  because timer resolution can hide a short fit.
- Log scales are explicit and reserved for quantities spanning orders of magnitude,
  such as integration errors. The 1e-13 display floor in the quadrature-error plot
  is disclosed; it never changes stored numerical measurements.
- Error-versus-reference figures use a zero reference line and label any unit
  multiplier. Agreement plots are not residual or model-adequacy diagnostics.

These conventions use ggplot2's [shared themes](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/theme.html)
and [explicit export controls](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggsave.html).
Each figure is saved as selectable-text **SVG** and a **160-dpi PNG**, with
fixed dimensions recorded in the [figure manifest](figures/manifest.json).
Font family is generic sans-serif; the resolved font can differ across platforms.

## Generate figures without running fits or benchmarks

Install the documentation-only R packages:

```r
install.packages(c("ggplot2", "jsonlite", "svglite"),
                 repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
```

From the repository root:

```sh
Rscript docs/figures/render.R --all
# Or render an individual family/figure:
Rscript docs/figures/render.R ols
Rscript docs/figures/render.R approximation
Rscript docs/figures/render.R sleepstudy
./scripts/render-docs
```

The renderer reads saved benchmark/reference reports and notebook-exported
points in `figures/data/`. It does not call estimators, regenerate reference
fixtures or run timed workers. A changed numerical report requires refreshed
plots; unchanged measurements should not be retimed for a style change.

The [manifest](figures/manifest.json) records each input path/content MD5, image
hashes, dimensions, renderer/theme hashes, R version, platform and direct package
versions. [The R package record](figures/r-packages.json) also records installed
transitive dependency versions. These are the versions used for the saved figures;
installing another version is not a claim of byte-identical reproduction.
Data/report provenance remains in its original statistical verification records.

Mathematical profile and posterior plots use points exported by the executable
walkthroughs, preserving the visible calculations. Re-executing those .qmd pages
updates their small JSON point snapshots and figures. Other figures read existing
result reports. Jupyter embeds SVGs with namespaced clip IDs so figures on the same
page do not interfere with each other.

Ordinary website rendering reuses frozen outputs and saved images. Neither R
nor Python is required to browse the committed HTML. Re-executing computational
notebooks still requires the [documentation environment](documentation.qmd).

## Existing figure coverage

The common renderer covers all five fixed/Gaussian-intercept benchmarks, the
logistic-mixed benchmark, v0.1 preservation comparisons, Gaussian likelihood
profiles, published-data numerical agreement, sleepstudy random slopes,
logistic-mixed integration error, node sensitivity and conditional posterior shape.
SVG and PNG downloads are retained alongside their saved input records.
